title: Bitcoin analytics application with REST updates, ten dashboards, update calendar and registry
runPolicy: Run once per host and profile in a fresh host session with the installed plugin; repeat 3 times for speed statistics only after the quality outcome is stable.
The agent performs creation and deployment; operator and harness checks are performed by the tester and read-only harness, never by the agent.
A failed critical check (critical: true) fails the scenario; speed results of a failed scenario are reported but excluded from comparison.
Browser checks (P11) run only because this scenario explicitly requests browser verification; record observations separately from import results.
Fixture mode is the oracle source. Live API checks are optional and never replace fixture assertions.

authorization.scope: Create and deploy one new identified DEV/QA/TEST application (alias btc-dashboard) with its BTC_% schema objects, migrations, packages and scheduler jobs in the identified workspace and parsing schema.
excluded: changes to other applications or non-BTC_% objects
workspace users, workspace authentication settings, ACLs, wallets and grants
authorization.remoteRule: Remote targets: dangerous database operations need exact-plan human confirmation (docs/deployment-safety.md).
authorization.localRule: Actual local non-production targets: task-scoped database changes allowed without separate confirmation.

agentPrompt.uk: Створи окремий APEX застосунок "Bitcoin Dashboard" (alias btc-dashboard, ID {applicationId}) у тестовому середовищі {env} зі стандартною автентифікацією Oracle APEX Accounts. Створи таблиці для курсів, денних агрегатів, розкладів і реєстру оновлень; PL/SQL пакети для оновлення курсу bitcoin через REST API CoinGecko (USD і EUR) з режимом fixture для тестів, логуванням кожного запуску і розкладом через DBMS_SCHEDULER. Зроби 10 різних аналітичних дашбордів (огляд ринку, історія з ковзними середніми, OHLC, волатильність, розподіл доходностей, місячна дохідність, просідання від ATH, обсяги, сезонність, технічні індикатори RSI/MACD), календар оновлень (фактичні і заплановані запуски) та реєстр оновлень з деталями запуску і кнопкою ручного оновлення для адміністратора (група BTC_ADMINS). Контракт fixture-режиму: відповіді API зберігаються в таблиці BTC_FIXTURE_PAYLOADS за назвою варіанта; оператор завантажить історичний варіант HISTORY після розгортання, а запуск типу BACKFILL має його імпортувати; налаштування AS_OF_OVERRIDE, якщо задане, дашборди вважають поточним часом; усі розклади після розгортання вимкнені. Розгорни застосунок і перевір у браузері вхід, усі дашборди, календар і реєстр.
agentPrompt.en: Create a separate APEX application "Bitcoin Dashboard" (alias btc-dashboard, ID {applicationId}) in the test environment {env} with standard Oracle APEX Accounts authentication. Create tables for prices, daily aggregates, schedules and the update registry; PL/SQL packages that update the bitcoin price through the CoinGecko REST API (USD and EUR) with a fixture mode for tests, logging of every run and scheduling through DBMS_SCHEDULER. Build 10 different analytical dashboards (market overview, history with moving averages, OHLC, volatility, return distribution, monthly performance, drawdown from ATH, volume, seasonality, RSI/MACD technical indicators), an update calendar (actual and planned runs) and an update registry with run details and an admin-only manual update button (group BTC_ADMINS). Fixture-mode contract: API responses are stored in table BTC_FIXTURE_PAYLOADS by variant name; the operator loads the HISTORY variant after deployment and a BACKFILL run must ingest it; when the AS_OF_OVERRIDE setting is set, dashboards treat it as now; all schedules are disabled after deployment. Deploy the application and verify login, all dashboards, the calendar and the registry in the browser.

tables.name: BTC_SOURCES
tables.columns: source_id NUMBER identity PK; code VARCHAR2(30) UNIQUE NOT NULL; name VARCHAR2(100) NOT NULL; base_url VARCHAR2(400) NOT NULL; is_active CHAR(1) DEFAULT Y CHECK (Y,N)

tables.name: BTC_CURRENCIES
tables.columns: currency_code VARCHAR2(3) PK CHECK upper; name VARCHAR2(50) NOT NULL; symbol VARCHAR2(5); is_active CHAR(1) DEFAULT Y CHECK (Y,N)

tables.name: BTC_PRICE_TICKS
tables.columns: tick_id NUMBER identity PK; source_id FK BTC_SOURCES NOT NULL; currency_code FK BTC_CURRENCIES NOT NULL; observed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL; price NUMBER(20,8) NOT NULL CHECK > 0; market_cap NUMBER(24,2); volume_24h NUMBER(24,2); change_24h_pct NUMBER(10,4); run_id NUMBER NULL (FK to BTC_UPDATE_RUNS added in V003); created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT systimestamp; UNIQUE (source_id, currency_code, observed_at)

tables.name: BTC_PRICE_DAILY
tables.columns: currency_code FK; price_day DATE; open_price, high_price, low_price, close_price, avg_price NUMBER(20,8) NOT NULL; volume NUMBER(24,2); tick_count NUMBER NOT NULL; updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE; PK (currency_code, price_day); CHECK low <= open/close <= high

tables.name: BTC_UPDATE_SCHEDULES
tables.columns: schedule_id NUMBER identity PK; name VARCHAR2(60) UNIQUE NOT NULL; repeat_interval VARCHAR2(400) NOT NULL; time_zone VARCHAR2(64) DEFAULT UTC; update_kind VARCHAR2(20) CHECK (CURRENT, HISTORY, BACKFILL); is_enabled CHAR(1) DEFAULT N CHECK (Y,N); job_name VARCHAR2(128) UNIQUE; created_by, created_at, updated_by, updated_at

tables.name: BTC_UPDATE_RUNS
tables.columns: run_id NUMBER identity PK; schedule_id FK NULL; trigger_type VARCHAR2(20) CHECK (MANUAL, SCHEDULED, BACKFILL, FIXTURE); provider_mode VARCHAR2(10) CHECK (LIVE, FIXTURE); status VARCHAR2(20) CHECK (RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, SKIPPED); started_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL; finished_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE; duration_ms NUMBER; http_status NUMBER(3); request_url VARCHAR2(1000); rows_received, rows_inserted, rows_skipped NUMBER DEFAULT 0; payload_hash VARCHAR2(64); error_code VARCHAR2(20); error_message VARCHAR2(4000); created_by VARCHAR2(255)

tables.name: BTC_SETTINGS
tables.columns: setting_key VARCHAR2(60) PK; setting_value VARCHAR2(1000); description VARCHAR2(400); keys: PROVIDER_MODE, API_BASE_URL, HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, WALLET_PATH, CREDENTIAL_STATIC_ID, DEFAULT_CURRENCY, CURRENCY_ALLOW_LIST, RETENTION_DAYS, FIXTURE_VARIANT, AS_OF_OVERRIDE (timestamp; when set, dashboards treat it as now)

tables.name: BTC_FIXTURE_PAYLOADS
tables.columns: variant VARCHAR2(30) PK; kind VARCHAR2(20); http_status NUMBER(3); payload CLOB CHECK (payload IS JSON) or NULL for timeout; description VARCHAR2(400)

views.V_BTC_DAILY_RETURNS: daily simple and log returns per currency from BTC_PRICE_DAILY
views.V_BTC_VOLATILITY_30D: rolling 30-day stddev of log returns * sqrt(365)
views.V_BTC_DRAWDOWN: running ATH (MAX OVER) and drawdown % per day
views.V_BTC_RSI14: Wilder RSI(14) and MACD(12,26,9) per day
views.V_BTC_MONTHLY_RETURNS: month-end to month-end returns and yearly totals
views.V_BTC_WEEKDAY_HOUR: average hourly return by ISO weekday and UTC hour
views.V_BTC_RUN_STATS: runs per day by status, success rate, average duration
views.V_BTC_CALENDAR_EVENTS: union of actual runs and planned occurrences for enabled schedules (next 31 days) with event type, status and CSS class

BTC_API_PKG: fetch_current(p_currencies in varchar2 default null) return number  -- run_id
fetch_history(p_currency in varchar2, p_days in pls_integer) return number
ingest_payload(p_payload in clob, p_kind in varchar2, p_run_id in number) return pls_integer  -- inserted rows
rebuild_daily(p_currency in varchar2, p_from in date, p_to in date)
BTC_UPDATE_PKG: run_update(p_trigger in varchar2, p_schedule_id in number default null) return number
finish_run(p_run_id, p_status, p_error_code, p_error_message, counts...)  -- autonomous
BTC_SCHEDULE_PKG: create_schedule(p_name, p_repeat_interval, p_update_kind, p_time_zone default UTC) return number
validate_interval(p_repeat_interval) return varchar2  -- null when valid
next_occurrences(p_schedule_id, p_from timestamp with time zone, p_count pls_integer) return a pipelined/collection type
BTC_ANALYTICS_PKG: kpi_snapshot(p_currency) return sys_refcursor or pipelined row
range_bounds(p_range in varchar2, p_from out date, p_to out date)

fixtureSpec.usdModel: geometric Brownian motion, S0 = 62000, annual drift 0.35, annual volatility 0.60, hourly steps, seeded PRNG (xoshiro128** or mulberry32, record which)
fixtureSpec.eurModel: USD price x daily FX (EURUSD inverse) random walk around 0.92 with 0.3% daily volatility, same seed stream
fixtureSpec.volumeModel: lognormal around 3.0e10 USD per 24h with weekday factor
expectedValues: return_stats (mean, median, stddev, skew, best_day, worst_day)
kpi_last (price, change_24h_pct, market_cap, volume_24h per currency)
fixtureSpec.expectedValuesRule: This list is canonical. BTC-004 computes every item; BTC-111 compares every item; a dashboard oracle may reference only items from this list.
fixtureSpec.tolerance: 1e-6 relative for derived numbers; exact for counts and dates

critical: no hard-coded credentials or wallet passwords
bind variables or DBMS_ASSERT for any dynamic SQL
error handling records FAILED runs and never swallows exceptions silently
idempotent ingest on the unique key
UTC storage with explicit time zone conversion for display
major: set-based SQL for aggregation and analytics
constants for error codes and settings keys
instrumentation via APEX_DEBUG or logging with run_id

metricsCollected: scenario wall time and per-phase wall time
agent turns and tool calls by tool
browser page load time and console errors per page

phases.title: PL/SQL packages and REST API integration
Data load, scheduler and update registry
Update calendar and update registry pages

checks.title: Exact target and profile identification
steps: Read test.env literally; run doctor, connection_list and connection_test for the saved connection.
Read APEX_RELEASE, APEX_WORKSPACES and APEX_APPLICATIONS read-only.
Choose an application ID that is unused in the workspace (default 26101 on 26.1, 26201 on 26.2) and record it.
expected: Database/service/schema, workspace and APEX release (26.1.x or 26.2.x) match the profile.
The new application ID and alias btc-dashboard are free in the workspace; the target is DEV/QA/TEST and not production-marked.
Locality (local or remote) is recorded; it decides the dangerous-operation confirmation rule (BTC-034).
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Schema privileges and quotas
steps: Read USER_SYS_PRIVS, ROLE_SYS_PRIVS and USER_TS_QUOTAS read-only.
expected: CREATE TABLE, VIEW, SEQUENCE, PROCEDURE, TYPE and JOB are available to the parsing schema; tablespace quota is at least 200 MiB.

Optional capabilities are recorded as available or absent: EXECUTE on DBMS_LOCK (BTC-043 then uses the status-check alternative) and a PLAN_TABLE or EXPLAIN PLAN privilege (BTC-142 plan assertion otherwise not_run).
Missing privileges are reported as blocked with the exact privilege; the agent never grants privileges itself.
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Outbound HTTPS prerequisites for live mode
steps: Operator verifies (outside the agent) a network ACL for api.coingecko.com:443 granted to the APEX engine/parsing schema and an HTTPS wallet or the database system certificate store.
Record whether live mode is available.
expected: Live mode is marked available or blocked with the reason. Fixture mode is always available and is the default oracle source.
The agent does not create ACLs, wallets or grants (privilege changes are outside task scope).
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Deterministic fixture dataset
steps: Generate the fixture with fixtureSpec (seed 20261011): 730 days of hourly USD ticks, EUR ticks via a daily FX series, 24h volume and market cap; also the negative payload variants.

Compute every item of fixtureSpec.expectedValues in Node for USD and EUR, for ranges 30D and 1Y where range-dependent, and store them as private expected values with the formulas used (Wilder RSI, EMA-based MACD, sample stddev, log returns).
expected: Fixture JSON files and expected values exist in the private evidence directory with SHA-256 digests.
Regeneration with the same seed reproduces identical digests.
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: APEX end users for standard authentication
steps: Operator creates (or confirms) workspace user group BTC_ADMINS and two workspace end users before the run: BTC_ADMIN_USER (member of BTC_ADMINS) and BTC_VIEWER_USER; passwords are kept only in ignored test.env.
expected: Both users can authenticate to the workspace; group membership is visible in APEX_WORKSPACE_GROUP_USERS.
The agent never creates users or groups and never changes workspace authentication settings; the application only references the group name.
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Clean starting point
steps: Read USER_OBJECTS for the BTC_% prefix and APEX_APPLICATIONS for alias btc-dashboard.
expected: No BTC_% object and no btc-dashboard application exist, or the run is marked as a re-run with the previous state recorded (no blind drop).
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Fixture delivery contract
steps: Record the contract the agent receives in the prompt: fixture payloads live in BTC_FIXTURE_PAYLOADS keyed by variant; the HISTORY variant holds the complete market_chart series per currency; PROVIDER_MODE=FIXTURE reads the variant named by FIXTURE_VARIANT; a BACKFILL run ingests HISTORY.
Keep the generated fixture files from BTC-004 ready for the operator load in BTC-050.
expected: The agent-authored migrations seed only the small negative variants (HTTP_429, HTTP_500, TIMEOUT, INVALID_JSON, EMPTY_PRICES) and leave HISTORY, GAP_6H, OUT_OF_ORDER and DUPLICATE for the operator load; no multi-megabyte CLOB is embedded in a frozen migration.
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Request understanding and plan
steps: Send agentPrompt verbatim in a fresh host session with the installed plugin.
expected: Before writing files, the agent states a concise plan covering: separate application, APEX Accounts authentication, tables, packages, scheduler, 10 dashboards, calendar, registry, deployment.
At most one clarifying question, and only about a genuinely missing fact (for example the application ID if BTC-001 left it ambiguous).
The agent does not ask again for import permission that the request already gives on a DEV/QA/TEST target.
evidence: agent turns, tool calls by tool, validate cycles and retries

checks.title: Reference and pattern usage before authoring
steps: Inspect tool calls before the first APEXlang file write.
expected: The agent consults plugin references/patterns for charts, cards, calendar, interactive report and modal form before authoring.
No complete manual is loaded into context; reference reads are bounded.
evidence: agent turns, tool calls by tool, validate cycles and retries

checks.title: HTTP integration design
steps: Review BTC_API_PKG body.
expected: HTTP uses APEX_WEB_SERVICE.MAKE_REST_REQUEST (or UTL_HTTP) with the base URL, timeout and optional wallet path/credential static ID read from BTC_SETTINGS; no hard-coded secret, key or password.
The request URL is built from validated currency codes (allow-list ISO codes) and constants; no user input is concatenated into SQL.
HTTP status, response size and elapsed time are recorded in BTC_UPDATE_RUNS; non-2xx responses raise a typed error (BTC-20001 to BTC-20009).
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Payload parsing and idempotent upsert
steps: Review INGEST_PAYLOAD.
expected: JSON is parsed with JSON_TABLE or APEX_JSON for both supported shapes (simple/price current and market_chart history).
Rows are merged on the unique key (source_id, currency_code, observed_at); re-ingesting the same payload inserts 0 rows and counts them as skipped.
Daily aggregation rebuilds only the affected days (open = first, close = last, high/low/avg/volume, tick count).
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Run logging and transaction boundaries
steps: Review BTC_UPDATE_PKG.
expected: START_RUN/FINISH_RUN use an autonomous transaction for the registry row only; tick data commits with the run outcome.
A failure records status FAILED with error code/message (max 4000 chars, no stack secrets) and leaves no partial ticks for that run.

Concurrent runs are prevented with a RUNNING-status check under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on a single BTC_SETTINGS row (or DBMS_LOCK when BTC-002 found it granted); a second concurrent run is recorded as SKIPPED.
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

checks.title: Provider modes
steps: Review BTC_SETTINGS and BTC_API_PKG.
expected: Setting PROVIDER_MODE switches between LIVE (HTTPS) and FIXTURE (payload from BTC_FIXTURE_PAYLOADS); the default after install is FIXTURE.
Fixture mode needs no network access.
evidence: sanitized result code and server postcondition

NEXT_OCCURRENCES(p_schedule_id, p_from, p_count) returns planned run times via DBMS_SCHEDULER.EVALUATE_CALENDAR_STRING; it is used by the calendar view.
Job action calls BTC_UPDATE_PKG.RUN_UPDATE(p_trigger => SCHEDULED, p_schedule_id => ...).
